# Decant

Ambient RNA decontamination for single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq,
with a differential expression test that models ambient RNA instead of
subtracting it. No other ambient RNA tool we found offers one.

**Documentation:** the [User
Guide](https://github.com/kroy3/Decant/wiki) covers installation, the
Seurat workflow, multi-sample data, differential expression and
diagnostics, chapter by chapter.

## What is new

1.  **Contamination-aware differential expression**
    ([`ambient_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_de.md),
    [`DecantDE()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/DecantDE.md)).
    When disease tissue releases more ambient RNA than controls, an
    abundant cell type’s disease genes leak into every other cell type
    and are reported as differentially expressed. Existing tools correct
    counts and then test. Decant puts each sample’s measured ambient
    RNA, and its uncertainty, inside the negative binomial model:
    `mu = native expression + ambient`. It supports covariates and is
    robust to outlier samples in large cohorts. **Status:
    experimental.** With shuffled labels on three real datasets it now
    rarely reports false hits, a little more often than standard edgeR;
    it has not yet been shown to beat a standard test on real data (see
    [Limits](#limits)).
2.  **Correction that keeps what cannot be ambient** (`bayes_cell`).
    Counts far above what ambient RNA could produce in a cell (doublets,
    rare expressers) keep their molecules; only the expected ambient
    share is removed.
3.  **Never adds counts.** Corrected counts are bounded by the observed
    counts, checked on every run.
4.  **Every default is gated.** Each component must pass a falsification
    test against ground truth in CI. Components that failed are kept off
    and documented.

## How it compares

### Correction against experimental ground truth

Two datasets from the benchmark of Cargnelli et al. (2026), scored with
the paper’s metrics. Retain is the share of the cell’s own signal that
is kept, and removal the share of ambient signal removed, both per gene,
1 is best. Decant, SoupX and DecontX were run on the same inputs.
CellBender’s numbers are the paper’s own, not a run here.

|  | Decant | SoupX | DecontX | CellBender (published) |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| human/mouse mixture 20k: retain | 0.989 | 0.992 | 0.983 | 0.996 |
| human/mouse mixture 20k: **removal** | **0.616** | 0.345 | **0.722** | 0.729 |
| held-out mixtures 1k, 5k, 10k: retain (mean) | **0.992** | 0.982 | 0.984 | not run |
| held-out mixtures 1k, 5k, 10k: **removal** (mean) | **0.444** | 0.679 | **0.637** | not run |
| Smart-seq2, no ambient RNA: retain | 0.998 | 0.989 | 0.952 | 0.797 |

**Decant removes less ambient RNA than DecontX: 10 points less on the
20k mixture and 19 points less on held-out mixtures**, where its
contamination estimate is too low. It keeps more of the cells’ own
counts than DecontX and SoupX. It removes almost nothing where there is
nothing to remove. Its contamination estimate now matches the
cross-species truth (median 0.027 against 0.029; before this release
0.013). That mixture was used to find the estimator’s flaw; results on
held-out mixtures are in
[`validation/BENCHMARK.md`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/validation/BENCHMARK.md),
sections 1c and 1d.

### Correction: six tools on real 10x PBMC 4k data

Same cells, soup and clusters for every tool. “Ambient-compatible”
foreign counts are marker counts in cell types that do not express the
marker, at a level ambient RNA could explain; “not ambient” are those
too high to be ambient, mostly B-cell doublets. A good tool removes the
first and keeps the second.

|  | Decant | SoupX | DecontX | CellBender¹ | AmbiDose | scAR |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| ambient-compatible foreign counts removed | 88–95% | 76–94% | 97–100% | 54–98% | 67–79% | 99–100% |
| counts that are not ambient removed (lower is better) | 14–37% | 12–31% | 96–100% | 4–68% | 82–100% | 58–82% |
| native marker signal lost | 1–4% | 1–2% | 2–6% | 0–1% | 0–6% | 18–26% |
| counts added | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 727,390 |
| run time (4 CPU cores) | 11 s | 12 s | 34 s | 55 min | 73 s | 15 min |

¹ Reduced CPU configuration; CellBender is designed for a GPU.

Decant removes more ambient-compatible counts than SoupX and AmbiDose on
all three marker sets and than CellBender (as run here) on two of three.
It keeps the counts that are not ambient, which DecontX, AmbiDose and
scAR remove, and it is as fast as the fastest tool. DecontX removes 5 to
9 points more of the ambient-compatible counts. Details and caveats:
[`validation/BENCHMARK.md`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/validation/BENCHMARK.md).

### Differential expression (simulated case/control studies)

|  | leaked genes called (of 80), 6 vs 6 | null false-positive rate, 6 vs 6 | null false-positive rate, 50 vs 50, confounding batch |
|----|----|----|----|
| **`ambient_de`** | **0** | **0.05** | **0.05** |
| SoupX, then edgeR | 1.5 | 0.04 | not run |
| naive edgeR | 53 | 0.22 | 0.45 |
| naive Wilcoxon | not run | not run | 0.46 |
| subtract ambient, then Wilcoxon | not run | not run | 0.14 |

Nominal false-positive rate 0.05. In the 6 vs 6 study, correcting with
Decant’s `bayes` rule and then running edgeR was as good as
`ambient_de`; `ambient_de` is the option that stays valid with
covariates such as batch.

**Calibration on real data.** Condition labels shuffled between donors
so that there is nothing to find, 24 shuffles per cell type. A
calibrated test reports a hit in a few shuffles, and few genes when it
does.

| data, cell types | `ambient_de`: shuffles with a hit | most hits in one shuffle | naive edgeR: shuffles with a hit |
|----|----|----|----|
| GSE272082 brain, AD vs control; microglia, oligodendrocytes | 4 of 48 | 9 | 1 of 48 |
| GSE190015 brain, nine controls; microglia, oligodendrocytes | 5 of 48 | 1 | 3 of 48 |
| GSE273597 pancreas, T1D vs control; acinar | 1 of 24 | 1 | 0 of 24 |
| GSE273597 pancreas; ductal | 4 of 24 (before this release: 5, up to **2,300** genes) | 1 | 0 of 24 |
| GSE273597 pancreas; alpha | 6 of 24 | 5 | 4 of 24 |

On the pancreas data, for 6 of 23 donors the ductal ambient fraction
came out at 0.86 to 0.96 (the others 0.02 to 0.16): a single cell type’s
pseudobulk cannot always identify its own ambient fraction. The model
treated most of those donors’ counts as soup, and splits that separated
them gave over a thousand false hits. `ambient_de` now replaces a value
above `max_rho` (0.5) with the median of the other samples, adds their
spread to its uncertainty, and warns. That removed the false hits; it
changed nothing on the two brain datasets. The pancreas data were used
to find the problem, so they do not show the guard works elsewhere.
`ambient_de` is slightly more liberal than naive edgeR overall (hits in
20 of 168 shuffles against 8, never more than 9 genes). Details:
[`validation/BENCHMARK.md`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/validation/BENCHMARK.md),
sections 3b and 3c.

An earlier problem, the cause of hits in most shuffles on the brain data
(82 of 96 tests, up to 574 genes), was fixed by using edgeR’s trended
dispersion (section 3b).

## Install

``` r

remotes::install_github("kroy3/Decant")
```

## Quick start

The raw (unfiltered) matrix is required: its empty droplets measure the
ambient RNA.

``` r

library(Decant)
raw <- read_10x_counts("sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
cells <- colnames(read_10x_counts("sample/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))
d <- split_droplets(raw, cells = cells)
res <- decant(d$cells, d$empties, clusters = my_clusters)
res$corrected   # corrected counts, sparse
res$rho         # per-cell contamination
```

From Seurat:

``` r

obj <- RunDecant(obj, raw = "sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")  # new "Decant" assay

res <- DecantDE(obj, cell_type = "Microglia", sample_col = "donor",
                formula = ~ diagnosis, raw = raw_paths_by_donor)
subset(res, ambient_driven)   # hits a standard pipeline reports that the soup explains
```

## Limits

- Ground truth so far is four human/mouse mixtures and one negative
  control, all from cell lines. On the 10k mixture Decant underestimates
  contamination (0.021 against 0.062) and ranks cells poorly; DecontX
  does better there. The genotype mixture and the paper’s medium- and
  high-complexity datasets are not yet run.
- When the soup resembles the cells (a single cell type), contamination
  cannot be estimated from expression. Decant then warns and asks for
  `rho`; the number it reports in that case is not reliable.
- Memory: about 9.5 GB for 11,000 cells and 1.9 million empty droplets.
- **[`ambient_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_de.md)
  is experimental.** On real data it has been checked for calibration
  only (three datasets, shuffled labels); before this release it failed
  in pancreas ductal cells. That it removes ambient-driven hits a
  standard test reports is shown only in simulation, from a simulator
  that follows the model’s own mechanism. Two pre-registered real-data
  tests (pancreas, T1D vs control; brain regions within donors) could
  not show it: the standard test found no ambient-driven hits to remove
  (`validation/BENCHMARK.md`, 3c and 3d). Until there is real-data
  evidence, report `ambient_de` hits together with a standard pseudobulk
  test. Analyses made with earlier versions should be rerun.
- Empty droplets that over-represent genes the cells also express are
  not detected and make the contamination estimate too low.

The full scorecard, design notes and history are in
[`validation/SCORECARD.md`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/validation/SCORECARD.md);
changes are in [`NEWS.md`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/NEWS.md).

## Development

``` r
devtools::test()                              # unit tests
Rscript scripts/run_falsification_gates.R     # falsification gates (also run in CI)
Rscript scripts/check_user_guide.R            # run every example in the user guide
Rscript scripts/build_user_guide.R            # copy wiki/ into the website articles
# the GitHub wiki is updated from wiki/ by .github/workflows/wiki.yaml
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`DecantDE()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/DecantDE.md) :
  Contamination-aware DE for one cell type of a multi-sample Seurat
  object.

- [`RunDecant()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/RunDecant.md)
  : Run Decant on a Seurat object.

- [`ambient_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_de.md)
  : Contamination-aware differential expression on pseudobulk counts.

- [`ambient_global()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_global.md)
  : Global soup profile: normalised aggregate of the empty-droplet pool.

- [`ambient_structured()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_structured.md)
  : Structured soup profile (lysis diagnostic).

- [`cluster_basis()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/cluster_basis.md)
  : Derive a program basis (cluster mean profiles) from the observed
  cells.

- [`correct_counts()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/correct_counts.md)
  : Remove ambient counts from each cell (mass-conserving).

- [`correct_splice_aware()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/correct_splice_aware.md)
  : Splice-aware layer decontamination.

- [`correct_total_then_split()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/correct_total_then_split.md)
  : Baseline to beat: correct the TOTAL, then split the removal by each
  cell's own observed unspliced/spliced ratio (what you get if you
  decontaminate total and naively apportion to layers).

- [`de_ambient_aware()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/de_ambient_aware.md)
  : Decant: test condition on OBSERVED data with the ambient load as a
  covariate, so condition-correlated ambient is absorbed instead of
  mistaken for signal.

- [`de_naive()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/de_naive.md) :
  Naive: subtract ambient point estimate, then test condition per gene.

- [`decant()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/decant.md) : Run
  Decant.

- [`decant_de_experimental()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/decant_de_experimental.md)
  :

  EXPERIMENTAL and OFF by default: failed its gate (made ambient-driven
  DE false positives worse via covariate collinearity). Kept only so the
  negative result is reproducible. Superseded by
  [`ambient_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/ambient_de.md)
  /
  [`DecantDE()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/DecantDE.md).

- [`decontx_em()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/decontx_em.md)
  : DecontX-style decontamination (Bayesian-mixture EM,
  reimplementation).

- [`estimate_rho()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/estimate_rho.md)
  : Legacy v0 per-cell rho estimator (superseded).

- [`estimate_rho_allelic()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/estimate_rho_allelic.md)
  : Allelic rho estimate. Fraction of mismatched-allele reads = rho \*
  P(soup read is from another donor). With pool abundances a_d, for a
  cell of donor d that probability is (1 - a_d). Invert to recover rho.

- [`estimate_rho_cluster()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/estimate_rho_cluster.md)
  : Cluster-pooled, absent-gene rho estimator with per-cell shrinkage.

- [`gate_allelic()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_allelic.md)
  : GATE: allelic rho error vs a marker-style proxy (here: assuming
  uniform pool, the naive 1/n_donors correction a non-allelic method
  would implicitly make).

- [`gate_ambient_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_ambient_de.md)
  : GATE: does contamination-aware DE stop ambient leakage while staying
  calibrated and powerful?

- [`gate_ambient_de_cohort()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_ambient_de_cohort.md)
  : GATE: does contamination-aware DE stay calibrated in large cohorts
  whose counts are not negative binomial?

- [`gate_correction()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_correction.md)
  : GATE: which mass-conserving correction rule is closest to truth?

- [`gate_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_de.md) :
  GATE: false-positive rate on ambient-trap genes (should be low for
  Decant, inflated for naive) while preserving power on true_de genes.
  Also reports the NULL-gene false-positive rate: if that is not near
  alpha the simulator or normalisation is broken and the gate result is
  meaningless.

- [`gate_diagnose()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_diagnose.md)
  : GATE: with a clean (oracle) program basis, do recovered lysis
  weights track the true lysis weights? Reported as rank correlation;
  clustering noise lowers this in real use.

- [`gate_hier()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_hier.md)
  : GATE: for empty-poor samples, is the pooled soup closer to truth
  than the independent estimate? For empty-rich samples, are they about
  equal (pooling should not hurt)?

- [`gate_rho()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_rho.md) :
  GATE: is the cluster/absent-gene rho estimator calibrated, and better
  than the legacy marker-ratio estimator?

- [`gate_splice()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gate_splice.md)
  : GATE: does splice-aware beat total-then-split on per-layer recovery,
  and does it correctly NOT help when ambient is not splice-distinct
  (negative control)?

- [`gene_species()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/gene_species.md)
  : Species of each gene from a species-prefixed feature name.

- [`pool_soup()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/pool_soup.md)
  : Empirical-Bayes-style shrinkage of per-sample soup profiles.

- [`print(`*`<decant>`*`)`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/print.decant.md)
  : Print a decant result.

- [`quick_labels()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/quick_labels.md)
  : Default clustering used when the caller supplies none.

- [`read_10x_counts()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/read_10x_counts.md)
  : Read a 10x Genomics matrix directory into a sparse matrix.

- [`run_benchmark()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/run_benchmark.md)
  : Global vs structured soup benchmark.

- [`score_correction()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/score_correction.md)
  : Score a corrected matrix against ground truth.

- [`score_species_mix()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/score_species_mix.md)
  : Score decontamination on a species-mixing experiment (full matrix).

- [`simulate_allelic()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_allelic.md)
  : Simulate a pooled multi-genotype experiment with allele-resolved SNP
  genes.

- [`simulate_ambient_cohort()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_ambient_cohort.md)
  : Simulate a large case/control cohort at the pseudobulk level.

- [`simulate_ambient_study()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_ambient_study.md)
  : Simulate a case/control single-cell study with sample-specific soup.

- [`simulate_de()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_de.md)
  : Self-contained pseudobulk DE simulator with three gene classes: null
  : no difference anywhere true_de : differs in NATIVE expression
  between conditions (real signal) ambient_de: native identical, but
  SOUP differs between conditions (a trap)

- [`simulate_experiment()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_experiment.md)
  : Simulate a contaminated droplet experiment with known ground truth.

- [`simulate_multimodal()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/simulate_multimodal.md)
  : Multi-sample, splice-resolved contaminated experiment with ground
  truth.

- [`soup_eb()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/soup_eb.md) :
  Empirical-Bayes soup profiles per sample.

- [`soup_profile_error()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/soup_profile_error.md)
  : Soup-profile recovery error.

- [`species_mix_hidden()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/species_mix_hidden.md)
  : Hidden-species view of a mixture: one species' cells, only its
  genes.

- [`species_mix_truth()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/species_mix_truth.md)
  : Ground-truth contamination from a two-species mixture.

- [`split_droplets()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/split_droplets.md)
  : Split a raw droplet matrix into cells and empty droplets.

- [`summarise_benchmark()`](https://kroy3.github.io/Decant/reference/summarise_benchmark.md)
  : Aggregate to mean +/- sd per (method, soup_bias).
